title: ptpt — split-flap (patapata) departure-board displays for the web

hero.heading: patapata
hero.tagline: A small library for split-flap displays on the web — the airport departure board, the Solari di Udine, the Vestaboard, recreated in the browser. The point is the *wait*: ptpt keeps the analog ticking on purpose.

problem.heading: Why split-flap
problem.body: A split-flap board doesn't just show a value — it *arrives* at one. The flaps tick through every glyph in between, and the wait is the whole experience. ptpt treats that delay as a feature, not a cost: text and images flip through the same `Frame` vocabulary, a `Cell` is one flapping unit, and a `Board` staggers a row of them so the whole display ripples like the real thing. A framework-agnostic core, with paper-thin wrappers on top.

family.heading: Five packages
family.description: At the center is `@love-rox/ptpt-core`, a framework-agnostic, zero-dependency engine (~3 KB gzip, ESM, ships its own `styles.css`). Pick whichever adapter (or adapters) suits your stack — `core` is pulled in automatically as a dependency.

core.name: @love-rox/ptpt-core
core.description: The engine — `createCell`, `createBoard`, frames, presets, and delays. Zero dependencies, ESM, ~3 KB gzip, with pure functions like `computeFlipPath` exported for the curious. Every adapter is built on this.

react.name: @love-rox/ptpt-react
react.description: `<Patapata>`, `<PatapataBoard>`, and the `useFlipCell` hook. Client components (`"use client"`), so they slot into RSC setups like Waku and Next.js.

vue.name: @love-rox/ptpt-vue
vue.description: The same `<Patapata>` / `<PatapataBoard>` API for Vue 3, plus a `useFlipCell` composable — identical options, identical behavior.

rehype.name: @love-rox/ptpt-rehype
rehype.description: Turns marked Markdown / HTML into split-flap boards. Emits readable text with `data-ptpt-*` at build time, then a `hydrate` helper animates it — no JS, still readable.

astro.name: @love-rox/ptpt-astro
astro.description: Wires up the Markdown plugin, injects the stylesheet, and runs the hydrator for you. Ships `Patapata.astro` and `PatapataBoard.astro` to drop a board straight into a template.

shared.heading: One stylesheet everywhere
shared.description: Import `@love-rox/ptpt-core/styles.css` once and every board gets a working dark split-flap look. Everything is themeable through custom properties on `.ptpt-cell` — width, height, flap duration, colors — or go fully headless and target the classes yourself.

behavior.heading: What's true across the board
items: **Frames** are the flaps — text, image, or `element` — each addressed by a `slug`; a bare string is normalized to a text frame.
A `Board` is one `role="status"` live region: cells are `aria-hidden`, and only the settled result is announced to screen readers.
`prefers-reduced-motion` is honored automatically — `reducedMotion: 'instant'` snaps to the target without animating.
Presets and delay functions ship as tree-shakable subpaths, so adding more never grows your bundle.
Pass a `PresetDefinition` object to a preset, not a bare string — a string is read as literal flap characters, not a preset name.

browser.heading: Browser support
browser.body: The flip is built from `transform: rotateX()` and a moving `box-shadow` on three stacked half-cells — standard CSS supported across all modern browsers. No 3D libraries, no canvas, no dependencies.

versioning.heading: Shared version line
versioning.body: All five packages release on the same shared version line, anchored to `@love-rox/ptpt-core`. Whenever any one of them changes, the others move to the same number — so you never have to wonder whether `react@0.2.5` is compatible with `core@0.3.0`.

cta.heading: See it in action
cta.body: The interactive demo lets you pick a preset and a flip mode, then watch a row of cells ripple to the next destination — just like a real departure board.
